addms72438-f107.summary: A woman's graphic-sign letter in English to a royalist officer: she had heard he was killed or taken, rejoices that he got safe to the King, and reproaches him for neglect after so many years' acquaintance. Deciphered with the lower alphabet of the neighbouring key sheet f. 106 (R8727), checked against the partial interlinear gloss; 122 of 128 words.

maurice1645.summary: Prince Maurice explains why he cannot bring his regiments to Rupert at Bristol, with the Scots army four miles from Worcester ('By your cipher, you may observe ...'). Not deciphered: no key in Add MS 72438 or in print fits the 93 groups.

addms72438-f9.summary: Intercepted royalist letter to 'My Lord', largely in a numerical cipher; not deciphered (no key of the volume fits).

addms72438-f10.summary: Intercepted letter to King Charles I, endorsed 'Quadrupl.' (fourth copy), in a numerical cipher; not deciphered.

r8433-trevor1645.summary: Arthur Trevor to Prince Rupert from Bristol, mostly clear (Sir Vivian Molineux, Sir Bryan O'Neile, the Prince of Wales's journey westward) with short numerical cipher passages; not deciphered.

addms72438-f104.summary: Charles I to the Prince of Wales (the endorsement '347 313 364' decodes as 'The King to the Prince of Wales'), a clerk's all-numeric fair copy, undated [1646?]: the King is content that the Prince has been referred to the Queen, and lays a command on him that no persuasion or threatening whatsoever make him [come into England?] before his father sends for him; a summons he has not really sent is to be judged by the Queen. Deciphered in part with George Lasry's key 'TNA SP106-8' (DECODE R924) and 35 values from R924's interlinear and this letter's contexts.

system: Royalist numeric nomenclators (two-digit figures for letters, about 100 to 398 in 1645 and to 697 in 1646 for words) in five documents; f. 107 is a simple graphic-sign substitution with a few homophones (key f. 106).
